files.purpose: Defines the Settings window: the SettingsPage enum (ten pages, each with a title, SF Symbol, sidebar tint and search keywords), the SettingsNavigation singleton through which the update notification and the relaunch after an install both open About (doc comment lines 82-83: "the update notification and the relaunch after an install both open About. Read once by the view, then cleared."), and the SettingsView shell (a 212-pt sidebar with a search field and page rows beside a detail sheet with scroll-driven chrome, fixed at 780x580). It also implements the private pages General, Appearance (split out of General in 1.6.2), Providers (signed-in providers first, each provider in a collapsible section), Source control, Archive and About, plus their helpers: SettingsSwitch, AppZoomCard (the app-wide zoom card, doc comment line 460), BackdropOpacitySlider, ProvidersRefreshButton, ArchiveDeleteAllButton, LicensesRow, MadeByDroppyRow, CreditLink, ProjectMarksRow and ThemePickerButton. The Hydra, MCP, Models and Shortcuts pages, the Token activity section and the About update rows are defined in other files and only placed here.

Doc comment (lines 460-461): "The app-wide zoom: Zoom out and Zoom in step through the levels, the stock size is a click away, and the percentage says where it sits." (so appZoom is an app-wide scale, not a chat-text-only size). The row sets no accessibility label or value (only the three buttons carry .help("Zoom out"), .help("Zoom in"), .help("Back to the stock size")). The reset button sits inline as the last HStack child with .disabled(current == 100) and .opacity(current == 100 ? 0 : 1), so it keeps its 22x22 slot while hidden; unlike BackdropOpacitySlider, whose reset lives in .overlay(alignment: .leading) with .offset(x: -28) and takes no room (lines 540-558). The zoom buttons set percent = AppZoom.next(percent, increasing: false/true); the reset sets percent = 100 with no withAnimation (the HStack's .animation(.snappy(duration: 0.2), value: current) animates it)

files.purpose: Implements the Shortcuts settings page: one card per AppShortcut.Section, each row naming a shortcut with a fixed-width recorder control, followed by a read-only "Composer" card listing six built-in chords that cannot be changed. It also contains the whole shortcut-recording machinery: the Keycap model and its drawn 3D keycap view, the popover that shows live keycaps with a verdict tint and Clear / Reset to default actions, and ShortcutRecordingSession, which installs a local NSEvent monitor, judges each chord against ShortcutStore on key-down and commits it 300 ms after every key is released.

The recorder Button toggles (`isPresenting.toggle()`, line 161), so a second click on the control closes the popover and, through .onChange(of: isPresenting), calls session.cancel(). Opening the popover (isPresenting true) calls session.begin with the Clear/Reset actions computed from the chord at that moment; closing it calls session.cancel(); the row's onDisappear also cancels

Clear action (id "clear", title "Clear", destructive) is offered only when a chord is set; Reset to default (id "reset", title "Reset to default") only when store.isCustomized(shortcut) and shortcut.defaultChord != nil

begin: closes any active session first, resets latched/heldKeyCode/verdict/message, seeds heldModifiers from NSEvent.modifierFlags intersected with KeyChord.allowedModifiers, shows caps, then installs the monitor for [.keyDown, .keyUp, .flagsChanged] and the resign-active observer

Monitor (lines 545-554): `guard let self, self.isActive else { return event }` passes every event through unchanged when the session is inactive; event types other than flagsChanged/keyDown/keyUp return the event; otherwise the handler runs and the event is swallowed (return nil). keyDown: repeats ignored (`guard !event.isARepeat`); `if keyCode == 53, flags.isEmpty { cancel(); return }` runs before `guard !isFinishing else { return }`, so plain Esc cancels even during the 300 ms commit wait; Esc with an allowed modifier is judged as an ordinary chord; otherwise (unless finishing) records heldKeyCode and heldModifiers = flags and judges KeyChord(keyCode:modifiers:)
judge: store.refusal(for: chord, replacing: shortcut) non-nil gives verdict .rejected with message = refusal text; nil gives .accepted and clears the message; the chord is latched either way

letGo runs when the last key and modifiers are released: accepted sets isFinishing, waits 300 ms (Task.sleep .milliseconds(300)), then if still active calls onCommit(latched) and closes; rejected clears the latch and returns to listening; listening just refreshes
flagsChanged: when no modifiers remain and no key is held, letGo; otherwise refresh caps; ignored while finishing (except for tracking heldModifiers)
keyUp only counts for the held key code; with no modifiers held it triggers letGo

refreshCaps (lines 659-674): `if let latched, verdict != .listening` shows Keycap.caps(for: latched); else `let modifiers = Keycap.modifierCaps(for: heldModifiers, phase: .pressed); if modifiers.isEmpty { next = [Keycap.ghostCommand] } else if let heldKeyCode { modifiers + key cap } else { modifiers + [Keycap.ghostKey] }`. So the single ghost ⌘ appears whenever no modifier is held, even while a key is held (when no latched non-listening verdict applies); the held key is shown only together with at least one modifier. caps are only reassigned when different
close() cancels finishTask, removes the monitor and observer, clears isActive/isFinishing and calls onClose once (which sets isPresenting = false)

files.purpose: Draws the "Token activity" heatmap that leads Settings > General: a header with Daily/Weekly/Cumulative mode chips, a one-canvas grid of week columns with square cells coloured on a five-step accent ladder, a strip of month labels, and a footer with the sum of every value in TokenLedger.shared.dailyTotals (`ledger.dailyTotals.values.reduce(0, +)`, line 91; this file applies no year filter, and whether dailyTotals holds only one year is decided in TokenLedger, which was not read; only the fallback tooltip "Total tokens recorded this year." says year) and a Less-to-More legend. It is plain page content, not a card, and keeps its mode view-local; the grid is rebuilt from TokenLedger.shared.dailyTotals only when the totals or the mode change, and a mode switch blends each cell from its old to its new colour over 0.45 s through an animatable modifier.

ui_elements: VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 10): header, heatmap, month strip, legend

Header: HStack(alignment: .firstTextBaseline, spacing: 12); "Token activity" (.title3 semibold, Chrome.primaryText, 1 line, header trait); Spacer(minLength: 12); one chip per mode with option.title (.body, weight .medium when selected else .regular), .buttonStyle(.chip(active: mode == option)), help text per mode, .accessibilityLabel(Text(verbatim: option.title)) (line 83), traits .isButton plus .isSelected when current; header .animation(.smooth(duration: 0.25), value: mode)

Mode help strings: daily "Each day on its own, against the busiest day of the year"; weekly "Each week as one shade, against the busiest week"; cumulative "The running total, so the year fills as it goes"

Heatmap: HeatmapCanvas, accessibilityHidden(true); cell = max(0, (width - 4 * (columns - 1)) / columns); height = max(1, cell * rows + 4 * (rows - 1)); cells are rounded rects radius 2 (continuous) at x = c * (cell + 4), y = r * (cell + 4); nil dates are skipped. Sizing (lines 213-224): HeatmapCanvas measures width with onGeometryChange into @State width (initially 0) and uses columns = max(grid.columns.count, 1), so before measurement cell = 0 and the frame height is max(1, 0 * rows + 4 * (rows - 1)); the Canvas (lines 247-251) recomputes cell from its own size.width with the real grid.columns.count and draws nothing when columns == 0 (`guard columns > 0`) or cell <= 0 (`guard cell > 0`)
Cell colours: future day Chrome.overlay(0.035); value 0 or maxValue 0 Chrome.overlay(0.07); fraction < 0.25 accent 0.32; < 0.5 accent 0.55; < 0.75 accent 0.8; else full accent

Month strip: Color.clear height 18; labels (.subheadline, secondaryText, fixedSize) centred at x = clamp(column * stride, 12, width - 12), y = 9, where stride = (width + 4) / max(columns, 1); placedTicks (lines 187-197) drops a label when its unclamped x = CGFloat(tick.column) * stride is less than 30 (TokenActivityStyle.minLabelAdvance) past the previously placed unclamped x; lastX starts at -30, so the first tick (for example one at column 0) is always placed; the clamp to [12, width - 12] applies only when drawing

Legend: HStack(spacing: 8) of summary "<tokens> tokens" (.subheadline, secondaryText, 1 line, tooltip = detail), Spacer(minLength: 12), "Less", five 10x10 rounded squares (radius 2) from the ladder, "More" (all .subheadline, secondaryText); accessibility element ignores children, label "Token activity", value = summary or "<summary>. <detail>" when uncertain tokens exist
feature_notes: Total is ledger.dailyTotals.values.reduce(0, +); uncertainTokens is ledger.uncertainTokensThisYear
Legend detail: when uncertainTokens > 0, "<UsagePanel.tokens(uncertainTokens)> tokens have an unknown source and may overlap imported history."; otherwise "Total tokens recorded this year."
Ladder squares use values [0, 1, 3, 5, 7] against maxValue 8, giving fractions 0, 0.125, 0.375, 0.625, 0.875: empty, accent 0.32, 0.55, 0.8, full accent

Mode switch: tapping the current mode does nothing; otherwise previousGrid = grid, then withAnimation(.smooth(duration: 0.45)) sets mode and switchCount = switchCount + 1, and on completion clears previousGrid only if no later switch happened

Blend math: HeatmapCanvas passes blend = Double(switchCount) and base = Double(switchCount - 1); progress = clamp(blend - base, 0, 1); while progress < 1 and previous exists and the column index is within previous.values, each cell's colour is old (progress <= 0) or old.mix(with: new, by: progress); the future flag comes from the current grid's date for both
The grid is built once per (dailyTotals, mode) pair so ledger updates while General is open do not redo a year of calendar work unless the totals change

B1->B2: header title .system(size: 15, weight: .semibold) became .system(.title3, weight: .semibold); mode chip labels size 13 became .body; month labels size 11 became .subheadline. (all size 11), and accessibility value "<total> tokens recorded" or "<total> tokens recorded, <n> of them without a kept source". 1.6.2 has one HStack with "<total> tokens", the uncertainty explanation moved into a hover tooltip ("<n> tokens have an unknown source and may overlap imported history." or "Total tokens recorded this year."), and accessibility value "<summary>. <detail>" or just the summary. The doc comment now says historical overlap stays in help and VoiceOver without crowding the footer
